operating-kit/ · the map · snapshot of 29 September 2026

The Operating Kit

One person decides, and a rotating crew of AI coding sessions does the rest, often several at once, none of them remembering the one before. The engine works because every session starts by reading a written record and ends by writing to it, and because each rule that matters lives in a file the harness loads, runs or tests. This page maps every part to its job and to the kit file that installs it. Anything in ‹angle quotes› is yours to fill.

The unit of work · hours

One session

Eight stations, the same every time, whatever the task. You step in at five points. Everything the session learns lands in one of four stores, so the next session starts from the record.

The unit of delivery · weeks

One track

How a feature goes from a question to every user. Work alternates between the sessions and you, and every crossing carries a named artifact, so you never rebuild context to answer.

The quality system

How a rule gets teeth

Four ways to bring judgment to bear, from softest to hardest. When the same class of mistake comes back, the check that should have caught it moves up a rung.

RememberedEnforced

Persona

A lens Claude adopts in context. A routing table says which lenses each surface expects, and the Definition of Done names them: N/A is fine, silence is not.

Fireswhen remembered; the sign off line makes it hard to forget
‹Primary user›: can I do this in ‹time budget› at my worst moment?
docs/personas.md from personas.template.md

Skill

Instructions in .claude/skills/‹name›/SKILL.md. The description lists the paths and words that matter, and Claude loads the body when the task matches.

Fireswhenever the task matches the description
ai-output-guardrails loads on any model output a user reads: one sample may raise a flag, never clear one.
3 skills and _skill-template

Subagent

A reviewer in .claude/agents/, in a fresh context: briefed, never shown the build conversation, so it cannot share its optimism. It returns a verdict.

Fireswhen invoked; the Definition of Done requires one for ‹your high stakes logic› and for access control
adversarial-reviewer must name the counterexample it tried. A bare ✓ is not a review.
5 reviewers in dot-claude/agents/

Guard

A test in guards/ that reads the source and fails the build. Where an exemption exists, it is a reasoned marker at the site or a registry entry in the guard.

Fireson every PR in required CI, and before each push through the git hook
A guard fails the build when raw error text can reach a screen a user reads.

A lesson's path, with project-nyx's example

  1. The mistake

    In project-nyx, CLAUDE.md was cut in half. Nine days later it was bigger than it had been two weeks before the cut, because nothing measured it.

  2. The lesson

    A budget without a structural fix only buys time, and a cap on count is not a cap on size (law L2).

  3. The rule

    Two lines in CLAUDE.md: an addition is paid for by a deletion. A pointer sends the reader to the story.

  4. The guard

    guards/claudeMdBudget.test.ts fails the build when the file outgrows its byte ceiling, or a trim leaves the ceiling stale. The ceiling is never raised to go green.

The parts that hold it together

Who decides what

Sessions, without asking‹Your principles›, ‹your value rule›, the hard constraints and ‹your safety invariants›. Small calls go in as defaults you can veto.
Sessions stop and askA non trivial BUILD plan; anything touching access control, deletion or export; a lens conflict; a spec edit; new scope.
Only youRulings, checks on a real device, store and console steps, and merges outside /dispatch.
Never, for anyoneDeploying except by merging. Committing to main.
Hand off once trustedA standing yes for low risk /dispatch rows; a dispatched PR merging itself when every check is green; deploy on merge.

Where state lives

What is in flight, and who has itTracker: In Progress, plus the claim comment naming the branch
What comes nextTracker: the project's run order; outside a track, Todo by priority
What is waiting on youTracker: one queue view; each item's first line is your single remaining step
How to build it correctlyGit: CLAUDE.md, the spec, the schema source
What happened, and whyGit: docs/sessions/ and the PR bodies
What is still undecidedGit: Open Questions in CLAUDE.md; resolved rows move to docs/decisions-archive.md
Why a rule existsGit: docs/operating-model.md and docs/engineering-lessons.md

STATUS.md is a pointer card no session writes to. A session edits CLAUDE.md on its own, inside the byte ratchet; a spec edit needs your yes; a frozen brief is corrected only by a dated addendum.

The clocks

Session start
The start hook unshallows a cloud clone, installs, prints the manual's byte count, and says RETRO DUE when it is.
Every push
A git hook runs the type check and the full suite. It can be skipped; CI cannot.
Every PR
Required checks on a main ruleset with an empty bypass list: types, tests, guards. The suite also runs in far time zones. A check that should only report gets its own workflow file.
Every merge
Squash. Every issue the PR names closes, so a task that spans PRs gets one sub-issue per PR. Server code deploys and writes its own record. Read back what closed.
Every migration
Its own PR with a safety preflight, applied before any code that needs it merges.
Every session
Claim, orient, work, /wrap: one PR, one record, the next prompt.
After a PR opens
At most one scheduled check, about 90 minutes out, only while sibling sessions are landing. Never at /wrap, never overnight.
Every mock round
Same URL each round. After you react, one proposal with a ledger mapping each reaction to what moved.
Weekly
The suite runs with the clock moved forward.
Every ~10 sessions
/retro, when the hook says RETRO DUE. Four questions; it must delete as much as it adds.

How you get briefed

Decision brief · format sample
DecidingWhether ‹feature› ships to everyone, or dark behind a flag first.
Options(a) Dark behind a flag, recommended: you try it on your own account and turn it off without a release. (b) To everyone: faster, and the only way back is a release.
Consequence(a) adds a flag check now and a removal PR at GA.
  • Rule from the brief alone. About four lines: options with one recommended, or the dissent named.
  • Conflicts come to you. Both sides are named, then the session stops until you rule.
  • Plan before code. A BUILD session posts its files and approach and waits; a DISCOVERY session never builds what it was asked to judge.
  • Mock what you change. A visual choice is drawn side by side, republished to the same URL each round.
  • A rule is a floor with a date on it. A better idea that breaks one arrives as a brief: the rule, its date, what it protected, the better thing.
  • Plain English first. Every issue opens with a TL;DR you can read cold, your one step in bold.
  • Two endings. Every push ends with a QA script you can run in three minutes; every session ends with one prompt ready to paste.

The twelve laws

  • Prose fires approximately never. A guard, a hook or a scheduled job has zero recorded misses. There is no third tier.L1
  • A budget without a structural fix only buys time. A cap on count is not a cap on size.L2
  • A file every session writes becomes a merge conflict magnet and only grows.L3
  • A queue with a mandated add and no mandated remove is the old checklist in a new store.L4
  • A deliverable only on an unmerged branch does not exist.L5
  • A scheduled wake needs an event it can miss, never a state a structural fix already prevents.L6
  • A detector that cannot fire looks exactly like a clean board.L7
  • Fan out the read, serialize the write. L8
  • Whatever performed an action writes the record of it, in the same run.L9
  • A check keyed on a signal your own arrival produces cannot tell you apart from a collision.L10
  • The isolated reviewer catches what the build conversation cannot.L11
  • Verify the premise at file:line before building on it.L12

The laws port; the numbers are tuned. 24 hours to stale, three in flight, a retro every ten sessions: defaults for one person running a few sessions a day. project-nyx once ran 26 in a day. Retune them at the first retro. Full text: docs/operating-model.md.

What goes wrong

  • A file every session writes. Parallel sessions edit the same lines, and a hurried resolution ships two versions of the truth. Give each session its own new file.
  • The rulebook regrows after every trim. A cap on the number of entries held while each entry kept growing. Only a byte ratchet in the test suite has held.
  • Your queue only grows. Sessions are told to add and nothing is told to remove. Design the drain before the queue, and clear it in sittings by kind.
  • A ritual written only as prose never fires. project-nyx ran its retro twice in over 500 sessions. Compute the trigger in the start hook.
  • A check that cannot fail reads as health. Break the source on purpose and watch every check fail once.
  • A PR closes issues it only mentioned. Every issue named in a title or body closes on merge. Name only what the PR finishes, then read back.
  • Deliverables strand on drafts. A session with no work PR opens its record PR ready to merge.
  • Mechanical fixes land and human ones do not. The board gets cleaner while your queue goes unread. Print the queue count where every session shows it.
  • The kit is a snapshot. The source keeps learning after the copy. Diff the kit against its source before you install it.

Installing it

Start here

Paste operating-kit/BOOTSTRAP.md §0 into the new repo's first session. It interviews you in four rounds, fills every ‹placeholder›, and installs the parts below as one PR, in roughly this order.

  1. A rulebook the agent loads every session.Roster, hard constraints, each convention as a rule plus its enforcement, the session protocol, the brief shape. Start near 20 KB; stories go in the lessons file.CLAUDE.md from CLAUDE.template.md
  2. A cast of lenses with a routing table.‹Primary user›, ‹ambiguity user› and ‹domain expert› among about ten, plus which lenses each surface expects.docs/personas.md from docs/personas.template.md
  3. A tracker where the issue is the spec.Newest comment wins. A claim comment names the branch; an outcome comment releases it. A queue view for you, an issue shape that opens with a TL;DR, a launch prompt that only routes.tracker settings, BOOTSTRAP.md §4
  4. A pointer card and one record per session.The card changes only when a track starts or ends. Each record is a new file, written once, saying shipped via #n.STATUS.md from STATUS.template.md; docs/sessions/README.md
  5. A start ritual and a close ritual./kickoff claims and orients; /wrap runs the done list, writes the record, releases the claim and writes the next prompt..claude/commands/: kickoff, wrap, handoff, pm-review
  6. Isolated reviewers for what can hurt someone.Each names the counterexample or attack it tried. Required for ‹your high stakes logic› and for access control..claude/agents/: five reviewers
  7. Invariants that load themselves.One skill per rule that must fire every time, with shipped code as the canonical example..claude/skills/: ai-output-guardrails, product-voice, backlog-groomer
  8. A narrow interface for you.Decision briefs, a mock of every visual change, a QA script per push, a paste ready prompt per session. You decide, try and merge.CLAUDE.md; docs/dev-handoff-runbook.md; docs/templates/mock-round-protocol.md
  9. A retro the start hook counts.The hook prints RETRO DUE every ten sessions. /retro answers four questions with numbers and writes a dated file that resets the count..claude/settings.json, .claude/hooks/session-start.sh, .claude/commands/retro.md
  10. A local gate and a server gate.Required CI on a main ruleset with an empty bypass list makes the fast checks binding. The kit has no push hook: copy project-nyx's..github/workflows/ci.yml from ci.yml.template; .githooks/pre-push
  11. A lessons file, and a guard for every mistake that comes back.The byte ratchet first. Then a guard each time a fixed rule breaks again, proven by breaking the source on purpose.docs/engineering-lessons.md; guards/ from the three .template files
  12. Orchestration, once there is work for it./dispatch turns a run order into sessions; /design-critique runs isolated lenses with a verifier each. Installed before there is work, they become ceremony.dispatch.md (take project-nyx's live copy; the kit's predates the standing yes), design-critique.md and its workflow
